detail: Research LinkedIn headshots, brand, job title, buyer intent for every registered operator. Updated multiple times/week — sometimes daily closer to the event.

Each operator lists their top 3 tech priorities at registration. Christina matches those to relevant client solutions and only surfaces matching intents in that client's dossier — e.g. if an operator lists CRM/CDP, Bicky sees them; if they list labor scheduling (not Bicky's solution), that's omitted.

Each client gets their own Notion page (not shared with other clients). Includes: intro, full agenda, attendee table with headshots/LinkedIn/brand/buyer intent, map layouts, team headshots, other client logos, and a section for their own account notes.

Ask client to nominate: 5 tier 1 targets (must meet), 5 tier 2 targets (backup), 10 current customers (advocates for seating), 20 detractors (must not sit with them). Built into the dossier as an interactive section.
Make the Notion page public, paste into Rebrandly and rename to a clean URL (e.g. go.858partners.com/create-bicky). Share with client alongside a note about the prioritization exercise.
Update attendee list multiple times/week with new registrations, cancellations, and walk-ins. Add table/room assignments once JG finalizes them.

Christina hands JG: top targets, tier 2 targets, current customers, detractors per client. JG uses Claude to assign tables/rooms based on floor and table/room capacity. Rule: each client table should have 1–2 tier 1/2 targets, 1 current customer, 0 detractors. Top targets sit left and right of the client; current customer sits across.

step: Review with clients on deal strategy call
detail: JG may walk clients through draft assignments during their deal strategy call and adjust based on feedback.
Once JG finalizes, Christina adds table/room assignments to each client's Notion dossier.

At check-in, the team inputs final attendee data (no-shows, walk-ins) into the Claude seating project and re-runs assignments if needed — e.g. if a client's tier 1 targets both no-showed, they need new neighbors.

A few days before the event, Christina builds a tracker per client showing their tier 1/2 targets, whether they share a table/room, and any gaps. Sent to Nic. ESMs use this onsite to make sure every client leaves with introductions to their targets.

step: Vet and sign photographer per city
detail: Each city has a preferred photographer once vetted. Fern and Christina handle the contract (hourly quote). Pre-event call if it's their first time working with 858.

Sent a few days before the event. Includes: all due dates, a full shot list, run of show (where to be and when), headshots of all attendees for reference, contact info, venue maps. Same doc goes to Robin.
Photographer delivers 20–40 edited photos by end of event day or early next morning. Must include all table/room linking shots. Candids and venue shots are a bonus.
Per contract (usually 3–7 business days). 200–1,000 photos including: speakers, entertainment, food/decor, venue, operator candids, team candids, client candids, and all table/room linking shots.
Robin gets the same photography dossier as the photographer. His start date is keyed to when the full gallery will be available.

step: Send full gallery + final attendee list
detail: Once the full gallery arrives, Christina sends it to Robin along with the final attendee list. If any walk-ins weren't in the original dossier, Christina researches their headshots first.

Robin creates one folder per operator (can be 50–200+ people). He goes through every photo and assigns each one to the relevant person's folder. Some operators have many photos; some just one or none. Takes ~2–4 days.
Christina confirms Robin is done and sends the organized folder to Chris. Christina and Chris approve Robin's invoice, then notify Fern to process payment.
Sent by Nic at project kickoff. High-level overview of what to expect, key links, and early to-dos for the client.
Nic sends the full event attendee list (Google Sheet). Clients check off 20 top targets they want 858 to invite to the activation. Chris then sends invites to those people.
Christina notifies clients when their dossier is ready. Includes the Rebrandly link and instructions for completing the prioritization exercise (tier 1/2 targets, current customers, detractors).
Fern drafts content → JG + Marty review → Christina builds in Figma → JG + Marty final review → Christina exports PDF → JG links and sends to all attendees + clients 2–3 days before the event.
Goes to clients only. Covers everything they need to know for the event: logistics, schedule, what to expect. Sometimes replaced by the program guide if that covers the same ground.
Christina opens the linking email document pre-event. JG, Marty, and Chris work on the copy. Chris stages a version with past photos and placeholder LinkedIn links so JG can see what it'll look like.
After the event, Chris takes the final attendee list and organizes emails around actual table/room assignments — removing no-shows, accounting for walk-ins.
Christina receives the same-day photo drop, organizes table/room linking shots into labeled Google Drive folders, and links Chris.
Chris inserts final photos and LinkedIn links per table/room. JG does one final review. Emails go out within 48 hours of the event — one per table for luncheons, one per room for bird circles.
Uses program guide, emails, event notes, and any other materials. Covers: what activations happened, how many people attended, any guest speakers, sponsor spotlights, and a thank-you to clients.
Nic layers in buyer intent reporting, satisfaction data, ESM debrief notes, and any feedback heard from operators or brand executives.
Final content edit and approval. Sometimes a 'what we can improve' section is added based on debrief feedback.
Once the full photo gallery is available and copy is approved, Christina builds the visual recap in Webflow using the existing template. A few rounds of review with JG + Marty.
Christina makes the Webflow link live and sends it to Chris. The link goes into every 1:1 follow-up email.
Christina creates the document structure, sometimes adds a Claude-drafted template as a starting point. JG and Chris own the actual copy.
Each email is personalized to the individual operator — references the event, includes a personal note from JG. Sent ~2 weeks post-event.
Once Robin finishes organizing, Christina sends the folder to Chris. Each operator gets a photo of themselves attached to their email.
Chris confirms photos and copy are complete for every operator. Sends individually, each with their photo and the live post-event recap link.
Fern handles venue contract and layout design — luxury lounge feel (think centurion lounge). Full bar, sushi, carving station, bra bar, high-end F&B throughout.
Full check-in system built for 858 House. Clients can reserve tables in advance for prospect meetings. Managed by Christina onsite.
Fern orders and coordinates any furniture needed beyond what the venue provides.
Always included. Fern coordinates using beans from a client if possible — e.g. Dutch Bros, Scooters Coffee.
858 House is a large operation. Fern coordinates extra staff for check-in, room management, and general support.
Fern handles venue contract and full catered lunch: salad, appetizer, main, dessert, drinks. Always includes espresso cart.
Usually JG and/or Mark Hatch from Informa intro the luncheon. Fern/Christina coordinate logistics.
Every seat assigned (not just tables) — see Seating & room assignments workflow. Clients get 1–2 tables with their assigned top targets, current customer, and zero detractors.
Two formats used: (1) catered lunch with networking time + sponsor introductions at tables, or (2) flip to a working session with structured questions and group discussion after lunch.
Usually 4–6 breakout rooms. Fern handles furniture, room layout, and vendor coordination.
Each room has a designated moderator — usually JG, Mark, or Caroline from Informa. Sometimes a client, Cody, or an outside expert (e.g. at RLC: someone from Bloomberg).
Attendees assigned to rooms by function, company size, or topic relevance. See Seating & room assignments workflow for full rules.
Regimented workshop: pre-set questions, ranking exercises, group discussion. Each table/sub-group nominates one person to share back to the room. Moderator floats between tables.
Rank your company's AI comfortability 1–4. Introductions. Questions for group discussion. One person per sub-group shares out.
~2 weeks before the event. Clients schedule with Nic. He walks through a full prep deck covering logistics, expectations, activation format, and what to expect onsite.
Clients schedule with JG. He strategizes on how to approach their top targets — talking points, what to know about specific operators, overall goals for the event.
Post-event. Nic hosts a feedback call with each client: what worked, what to improve, overall satisfaction. Notes go into the post-event recap.
Fern lets Christina know what collateral is needed — badges, note cards, directional signs, table cards, etc.
Christina designs all assets using existing templates and brand guidelines.
Fern reviews designs, approves, and coordinates printing/production through the relevant vendor.

GRIP is Informa's 1:1 speed-networking platform. Each 858 partner gets 10 back-to-back 10-minute meetings with qualified operators, scheduled by Informa based on mutual preference selections. The meetings run in a dedicated space (e.g. at B4, the Palos Verdes Terrace, 10:15am–12:45pm on Day 2).

Each partner assigns one person — their 'preference designator' — who will log into GRIP and make meeting selections on behalf of the company. Nic confirms this with each client. Deadline: ~6 weeks out.

Designator receives an email from Informa with login instructions. They log into GRIP and select up to 40 operators they want to meet with. Nic guides them to cross-reference their dossier tier 1/2 targets to prioritize strategically.

A few days before the final deadline, the designator reviews mutual interest signals in GRIP and adjusts selections. Note: this window often falls during the July 4 holiday week — flag early and push clients to act before the break.
Hard cutoff for all partner preference selections. After this Informa builds the schedule. Nothing can be changed after this point.
Informa publishes a draft meeting schedule. Nic reviews each client's 10 scheduled meetings and flags any conflicts or mismatches directly with Informa before the schedule is finalized.

step: Add finalized schedule to client dossiers
detail: Christina adds each client's 10 confirmed GRIP meetings (operator name, company, meeting time) to their Notion dossier so they can research each person and prep talking points in advance.

ESMs ensure each client is at their assigned meeting table on time. 10 back-to-back 10-minute meetings is a fast pace — ESMs help navigate transitions, flag no-shows, and keep clients focused. ESM tracker (built by Christina) includes GRIP meeting overlap.
Fern creates the initial project plan and holds all the workstreams early. Project kickoff meeting with full team.
Fern hands the project plan to Christina, who takes over day-to-day execution and accountability.

step: Monday — action items for the week
detail: Christina sends the team their action items for the week.
Christina sends a reminder for anything not yet completed that week.
Christina sends a preview of what's coming up the following week.
